intended_object: The universal-property lift for the quotient A/closure(nA) of a topological abelian group A: a continuous homomorphism f : A → B into a T1 topological group with n·f(a) = 0 for all a induces a continuous homomorphism A/closure(nA) → B. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The hypothesis KillsMultiples n f (∀ a, n • f a = 0) is equivalent to f vanishing on nA, because f(n•a) = n • f a. Since B is T1, {0} is closed, so ker f is closed and contains closure(nA). closedMultiples_le_ker proves exactly this via topologicalClosure_minimal. liftOfClosed then builds the map from QuotientAddGroup.lift, gets continuity from the quotient-map property, and satisfies lift(mk a) = f a by rfl. This is the standard induced map. The degenerate cases n = 0 (a vacuous hypothesis; maps into T1 targets kill the closure of 0 anyway) and n = 1 (f must be 0) behave correctly. The generality is natural: arbitrary topological abelian groups and any n. For a topological group B, T1 is exactly what makes {0} closed. The extra IsTopologicalAddGroup B instance from the section variables is cosmetic. Mathlib has the algebraic QuotientAddGroup.lift, which this builds on; I did not search Mathlib for a continuous version and know of none.
